newsitem.title: SPAIN: Cepsa says no plans to buy Iraqi crude.
newsitem.headline: Cepsa says no plans to buy Iraqi crude.

text.p: Spanish oil firm Cepsa has no plans to buy Iraqi crude although it would purchase it indirectly on the spot market, a spokesman told Reuters on Tuesday.
"We are not on the list of buyers for Iraqi crude, however it will be destined for the spot market and if it is in competitive conditions there, we will be interested," the spokesman said.
A trader at Cepsa said: "We have no contract with Iraq. We've got no problem with refining Iraqi crude on a spot basis but we have no term deal with them."
The United Nations partially lifted sanctions on Iraqi crude on Monday after a near-six year ban following its August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Iraq will be allowed to resume oil exports up to a total 2.0 billion dollars over six months to buy humanitarian goods.
